text:
ada: Heads-up — sketching a follow-up for encrypted safetensors streaming. main idea: lazy per-layer decrypt during warmup instead of full-file decrypt on hotstart.

morgan: sounds interesting. what are we optimizing for? CPU vs memory vs I/O?

ada: primarily memory + startup latency. decrypting entire checkpoint at hotstart kills memory headroom for big models. idea: keep shards encrypted on disk, stream and decrypt only requested layer bytes into ephemeral buffer, then copy to GPU / mmap when needed. fallback to full decrypt if low-bandwidth.

zane: tradeoffs: symmetric decrypt per-chunk adds CPU cost inside warmup path. do we decrypt on IO thread or worker thread?

ada: proposal: DecryptingTransport abstraction that sits between WeightSource and Loader. It provides async decrypt(chunk_id) and exposes chunk metadata: iv, key-rotation id. loader can schedule decrypt tasks on dedicated crypto pool.

olivia: how do we handle KMS/HSM integration? per-tenant keys + rotation? sounds risky for onprem.

ada: KMS integration is opt-in. Metadata header in safetensors sidecar contains key envelope and rotation pointer. DecryptingTransport consults local key cache and calls KMS unwrap only when encountering new rotation id.

morgan: caching policy: decrypted chunk lifetime? we need avoid double copies: prefer zero-copy into GPU when possible.

ada: two paths: mmap+in-place decrypt (if filesystem supports) or decrypt into pinned buffer then upload. prefer in-place where permitted by filesystem and kernel (requires decrypted file descriptor ephemeral). otherwise pinned upload.

zane: eviction & security: decrypted data must be zeroed on eviction. also consider enclaves: on-prem could use SGX/HSM.

olivia: what about warmup ordering? we should keep warmup hints (prefix tokens, attention hotspot) to prioritize decrypting early layers.

ada: yep. extend warmup hints protocol with decrypt-priority and chunk-granularity hints. warmup coordinator merges these with batching.

cipher-bot: Deploy check: crypto-pool size defaults: 4 threads, tunable per-dedicated cluster.

morgan: latency numbers? rough estimates?

ada: local AES-GCM decrypt cost ~0.8ms per 1MB on x86 (single thread). for a 10GB model in 4MB chunks, full decrypt single-threaded ~2000s. but lazy decrypt only touches ~10% => ~200s worst-case; with crypto-pool 16 threads and overlap with IO we get under 15s for hot-path.

zane: what's the interface change surface? minimal changes to Loader API?

ada: Loader gains async fetch_chunk(chunk_id) -> bytes | future; WeightSource returns encrypted_slice meta. DecryptingTransport implements fetch_chunk by fetching and decrypting. Existing code paths fall back to pre-decrypt if backend says decrypted=true.

olivia: long-term: unify with quantization pipeline — run decrypt -> dequantize -> upload as a streaming transform chain.

morgan: test plan?

ada: perf microbench for crypto pool, integration test with on-prem KMS simulator, e2e canary on Dedicated with opt-in flag. Need telemetry: decrypt latency histogram, key-unwrap counters, decrypted-bytes churn.

zane: security review required. we should write threat model and key-rotation playbook.

ada: I'll draft RFC follow-up with diagrams and a toy prototype in loader-experiments. anyone wants to co-author?

olivia: I'll help with KMS/HSM bits.

morgan: I'll own crypto pools and perf harness.

zane: I'll take loader integration and eviction semantics.

eng-ml-oncall: noted. tagging incident-watch for any regressions during canary.

ada: ok I'll push a short PR for the transport interface tomorrow. :thumbsup:
